correctness.rationale: For a quadratic target the schemes reduce to random affine recurrences, so stationary second moments obey an exact averaged discrete Lyapunov equation. Symbolic expansion gives the stated uniform-time and arbitrary-time coefficients. Independent finite-step quadrature of the exact correlated Brownian covariance converges to those coefficients. The no-go theorem follows algebraically from the necessary first- and second-moment conditions on the random time, and the Wasserstein lower bound follows from second moments under arbitrary couplings.

originality.rationale: The motivating source introduces LC-REI, unifies it with RMM and ALUM, proves non-asymptotic Wasserstein bounds, and reports long-time OU pathwise RMSE, but the inspected source does not state the stationary covariance expansion or the one-gradient covariance obstruction. Prior randomized-midpoint and Langevin invariant-measure papers establish stationary-bias analysis as an existing methodology, so the claim is restricted to the explicit new-method classification, arbitrary-time obstruction, and harmonic Wasserstein floor. No overlapping SCOPE record or accessible external source was found. Originality is only to the best of our knowledge, with contemporaneous follow-up risk.

value.rationale: The result separates transient/pathwise accuracy from equilibrium sampling accuracy for a newly proposed low-cost method, supplies sharp leading constants for configurational and kinetic bias, and proves that the RMM second-order covariance cancellation cannot be replicated within the natural one-gradient predictor family by tuning only random-time and predictor-noise choices. It also gives an explicit stationary configurational W2 lower bound for LC-REI on a harmonic target.
